subject: RFI: Key provenance & encryption artifacts for Project Helix
messages:
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@helixbank.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@helixbank.com
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Key provenance and encryption evidence request

Jordan,

Thanks for taking this — Helix is running an internal SIG/ISO readiness check ahead of our Q1 integration. A couple of items we need from Redwood to complete our control mapping: 

- A manifest of key material provenance for any infra where customer data is encrypted at rest (who created the key, KMS provider, rotation policy, and whether it's customer-managed or service-managed).
- A mapping document showing how your encryption controls map to SIG v2027 and ISO 27001:2013 controls (high level is fine).
- A short sample of audit logs that show key usage events (obfuscated sample OK).

Can you confirm whether Dedicated and Private deployments support customer‑managed keys (CMKs) and whether hosted (managed) deployments only use Redwood's managed KMS? Our procurement/security team will need this to sign off. Ideally we can get artifacts by next Tuesday (2027-12-07).

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Alan
Alan Cho
Lead Security Architect, Helix Financial
alan.cho@helixbank.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@helixbank.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Key provenance and encryption evidence request

Alan — thanks for the clear ask. Confirming receipt and we can provide the artifacts you listed. Quick answers up front: Dedicated and Private both support customer-managed keys (we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS); hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default but we offer an add-on for BYOK in some enterprise plans.

I'll coordinate artifacts with Security (cc'ing Marissa) and copy Sean for audit-log extraction. Targeting an artifact delivery by EOD 2027-12-08. If you need anything earlier for gating, tell me and we'll prioritize.

Next steps (short):
- Marissa will prepare the key provenance CSV and the mapping doc.
- Sean will provide an obfuscated audit-log sample.
- I'll send a consolidation email with attachments and the Drive link.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Office: +1 650-555-0199

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Action: Helix RFI artifacts (key provenance + logs)

Marissa / Sean — looping you in to fulfill Helix's artifact request. TL;DR: they need a key provenance manifest, a high-level control mapping (SIG/ISO), and an obfuscated audit-log sample showing KMS usage. Deadline: COB 2027-12-08.

Marissa — can you own the key-provenance CSV and the control mapping PDF? Items we should include in the CSV columns: environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), KMS provider, key creation date, created-by (service account or customer), CMK? (yes/no), rotation cadence, relevant evidence doc links. 

Sean — can you extract a small sample (max 200 lines) of key-usage events from November 2027 with any PII obfuscated? We only need the fields: timestamp, key_id (hashed), operation (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey), and requestor-principal. Attach as a plain .txt file.

I'll compile and send. Ping me if you need exceptions on timeline.

Thanks — Jordan

---
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@helixbank.com>
Cc: jordan.blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, sean.gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Key provenance and encryption evidence request

Alan — attaching the artifacts requested for Project Helix. Summary of what's included and short notes on provenance: 

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- redwood_kms_key_provenance_manifest.csv — CSV columns: environment, kms_provider, key_id (hashed), created_by, created_at, customer_managed (yes/no), rotation_policy, related_evidence_link. This covers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.
- soc2-encryption-control-map.pdf — High-level mapping between Redwood controls and SIG v2027 + ISO 27001 clauses. Callouts for controls that reference key management, key inventory, and key rotation.
- sample-audit-logs-2027-11.txt — Obfuscated sample of KMS API calls (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) from November 2027, redacted requestor-principals. Log format: ISO8601 timestamp | hashed-key-id | operation | region | requester-hash.

Key provenance summary (short):
- Dedicated and Private: support customer-managed keys (BYOK). Customers can bring keys from AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS; Redwood verifies key metadata during provisioning and stores only the key reference/ARN in our control plane. Rotation is customer-controlled; we surface rotation windows and validate key states on restart. Evidence: see CSV + provisioning API call sample.
- Hosted (managed): Redwood-managed KMS keys encrypt customer data at rest by default. Keys are created and rotated under Redwood's KMS tenant with documented rotation cadence. For customers requiring CMK for hosted, we offer an enterprise addon that integrates with a customer's cloud KMS — please let Jordan know and we can propose a timeline/quote.

A couple of notes on scope and limitations:
- The sample logs are limited in retention for hosted plans; Dedicated/Private retain longer depending on customer config (we've indicated retention in the control map PDF).
- For full, unredacted audit logs or HSM attestation material, we require an MSA addendum and an approved data access request (we can coordinate through your procurement).

Related links: project control map on Drive (shared link), HubSpot deal HLX-2027-023 for procurement notes.

If you'd like a 30-minute review call to walk through the CSV and the mapping, Jordan and I are available next week. Thanks — happy to answer follow-ups.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: redwood_kms_key_provenance_manifest.csv (CSV), soc2-encryption-control-map.pdf (PDF), sample-audit-logs-2027-11.txt (TXT)
